slides.page_title: Variables vs Locals vs Outputs vs Data

items: Data sources are read-only and DO land in state
Variables reach state only inside the resources using them
Variables and outputs take `sensitive = true`
Locals inherit sensitivity but cannot declare it

blocks.title: Reference Prefixes
items: `var.name`
`local.name`
`module.<name>.<output>`
`data.<type>.<name>`

spec.root: Where does the value come from?

items: Data source when the value exists and would be copy-pasted
Variable when it is a deliberate choice, not a discovered fact
Local when the same expression appears three times
Plain repetition when the expression is read once
Terraform has no global scope at all
A module gets values only through its own variables
Nothing leaks in sideways from the root

slides.page_title: Variables vs Locals vs Outputs vs Data (cont.)

blocks.q: Variable or data source for an AMI id?
a_bullets: Pinned by policy or ticket: variable
Copy-pasting a discovered id means data source

blocks.title: Anti-pattern
blocks.text: A variable whose value is always computed from another variable is not a variable. It is a local.

items: Writing `variable.foo`; the reference prefix is `var.`
The block keyword is never the reference prefix
Passing `null` still uses the default, surprising people
tfvars takes no expressions: `region = var.other` is invalid
Defaults must be constants: no account id lookups
`set(string)` where order matters — use `list(string)`
`any` on an input: error deep inside, no caller line
`optional()` outside an object type is invalid
Big integers drift: numbers are decimals rendered via JSON

lines: type = any             # error far from caller

items: A stray `*.auto.tfvars` loads silently and changes the plan
`TF_VAR_Region` does not set `var.region`; case matters
Committing `terraform.tfvars` with credentials, rotating nothing
Deleting a module output another workspace reads remotely

blocks.title: Breaks later, not now
blocks.text: A removed output only fails the consumer's next plan, long after your merge looked green.

items: Relying on interactive prompts inside a pipeline
No TTY, so the run waits forever
Always pass `-input=false` in automation

blocks.q: Plan says `Invalid value for input variable`. Where?
a_bullets: Type mismatch, caught before any API call
With `any` the message points inside the module
Type the input precisely and the caller gets blamed

blocks.title: Fast Fixes
items: `terraform console` to inspect resolved values
List `*.auto.tfvars` before blaming code
Last `-var` on the line always wins

blocks.text: Variables parameterize, locals compute, outputs publish. That triad is the whole module interface.

items: Primitives, then homogeneous collections, then shaped types
Prefer `object({...})` with `optional(k, default)` over `any`
Every public module input deserves a precise type
Validate early: `validation` plus `can(regex(...))`
Validate against reality: `precondition` / `postcondition`
`sensitive` hides output; `ephemeral` keeps out of state
Neither one encrypts the backend for you
Encrypt state, lock it, restrict access — the real boundary
`local.` for naming, tags and `for_each` maps
Outputs are return values and a stable contract
Ship typed variables, descriptions, validations, narrow outputs
`terraform console` shows what `var.x` and `local.y` resolved to

blocks.title: Trade-off summary
blocks.text: Strict typing and validation cost authoring time but move failures from apply-time to plan-time.

blocks.title: The final rule
blocks.text: Variables are what callers decide, locals are what you derive, outputs are what you promise.

caption.text: Part 2 of TERRAFORM I/O HANDBOOK. Half of all Terraform surprises are input plumbing: a stray `*.auto.tfvars` quietly changing a plan, `TF_VAR_Region` doing nothing, a sensitive value sitting in plaintext state anyway. This handbook walks the whole input/output chain — declarations, the type system, validation, the six-source precedence ladder, secret hygiene, locals and outputs. Save it before your next module review.
